signals.title: Meta Muse Glimmer: open-weight 30B agentic + function-calling model, runs on a single consumer GPU
signals.summary: Meta shipped Muse Glimmer on Aug 10 under a permissive (Apache-2.0) open-weight license: 30B, tuned for local agents, function calling, local coding, and LLM-as-judge. Quantizes under 20GB to fit a 24-32GB Mac M-series or RTX card, with speculative decoding for 1.5-3.1x speedups. Live day one on Hugging Face, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, plus hosted Together AI and Fireworks. Zuckerberg framed it as the US open-weight answer to Chinese labs. Corroborated by Meta's blog, Bloomberg, The Star, and a 298-pt HN front-page thread.
signals.run_with_it_note: Host it on Fireworks or Together and point a spare Twilio DID at it as the after-hours booking/FAQ brain for one business (NPB or DCKT). It's function-calling-optimized, which is the exact gap the old cheap-brain picks had: it can actually fire a check-availability or take-a-message tool call, not just chat. Owned weights, no vendor lock, and it lands the same week DeepSeek announced an API price hike.

signals.title: Google DeepMind WeatherNext: open-sourced weather + cyclone forecasting model, +24h lead time
signals.summary: DeepMind open-sourced WeatherNext (code + weights on GitHub, google-deepmind/weathernext). Forecasts general weather (temperature, precipitation, wind) plus cyclones up to 15 days out, with more than a full day of extra lead-time accuracy over conventional models. A WeatherNext 2-mini runs on a single TPU with a free Colab notebook. Surfaced via TLDR AI.
signals.run_with_it_note: David runs weather-dependent outdoor tours (kayak, pedal barge, swamp, booze cruise) where a bad go/no-go call costs a day of trips. Pull WeatherNext outputs for one region (Door County or Houston) and shadow-compare its next-day wind/precip call against NOAA for two weeks. If it wins the extra 24h, it becomes the model behind an automated cancellation/rebooking heads-up. This is the operator edge a software founder can't copy: he owns the trips the forecast is for.

signals.title: Docker Sandboxes: disposable, isolated sandboxes for AI agents
signals.summary: Docker shipped first-class disposable, isolated sandboxes purpose-built to run AI agents safely, one throwaway container per agent run. Hit HN front page at 329 pts on Aug 10. Containers are self-hostable and durable, so it's owned ground, not a rented platform.
signals.run_with_it_note: David runs a fleet of live agents (morning-brief, radar, graphify, ad ops) that touch real business systems across 12 vaults. Wrap one code-executing agent in a Docker Sandbox this week so a bad run can't reach Gmail/Twilio/ad accounts. Cheap blast-radius insurance before he scales agents wider.

signals.title: Qwen3.8 Max ranked #1 overall on the agentic index (confirmed proprietary)
signals.summary: Qwen3.8 Max is now rated the best overall model on Artificial Analysis's agentic index (545-pt HN thread, Aug 6). But it's confirmed proprietary/API-only, which answers last week's open question: the ownability that made it a provisional Spark isn't there. Demoted to Watch.
signals.run_with_it_note: Fine as a rented top-end brain for a one-off hard agent job, but not build-on ground. Was a Spark 2026-08-03; proprietary status drops it to Watch.

signals.title: Mistral Shieldstral: 3B open-weight multimodal moderation model
signals.summary: Mistral released Shieldstral, a 3B open-weight model for multimodal content moderation (text + images). 481 pts on HN. Small, owned, and self-hostable.
signals.run_with_it_note: Could screen inbound review replies, UGC photos, and social comments across the 12 brands before they auto-post. Owned and cheap, but needs a small build to wire in; Watch until there's a concrete pipeline for it.

signals.title: Vercel Agent Plugins: open 1.0 standard for packaging agent capabilities + MCP servers
signals.summary: Vercel published Agent Plugins v1.0.0, an open standard to package reusable agent capabilities and MCP servers into portable plugins. Surfaced via TLDR AI.
signals.run_with_it_note: David already runs a sprawl of MCP servers (opencx, twilio, gmail) and skills across vaults. A standard packaging format could turn his per-vault setup into reusable plugins, but the standard is a day old; watch whether it gets real adoption before betting on it.

signals.title: AMD acquires Taalas to etch AI models directly into silicon
signals.summary: AMD is buying Toronto's Taalas, which etches models into custom silicon to slash inference compute and memory. Huge HN momentum (937 pts). Fascinating for where inference cost is headed, but it's pure infrastructure, nothing David can build on. Fails the own-the-ground filter (score 1) so it can't be a Spark.

signals.title: DeepSeek announces it will raise API prices significantly
signals.summary: DeepSeek said it will raise API prices meaningfully, with roughly a 2-3 month runway before the hike. A reversal of the subsidized-price story that made DeepSeek V4 Flash last week's cheap-brain Spark. The weights are still MIT/open, so the owned-hosting path survives even if the hosted API gets pricier. This is the 'why now' behind moving to Muse Glimmer.

signals.title: Cloudflare Kitesurf: an agent-first browser running in Workers isolates
signals.summary: Cloudflare launched Kitesurf, a lightweight browser optimized for AI agents that runs inside V8 isolates on Workers. Surfaced via TLDR AI.

signals.title: LiquidAI LFM2.5-2.6B: compact open model for edge and lightweight agents
signals.summary: LiquidAI released LFM2.5-2.6B on Aug 4, a 2.6B open model aimed at edge and on-device lightweight-agent deployment. Small enough to run on a phone, which touches the desk-to-mobile theme, but too small for real business logic on its own.

signals.title: Prime Agent: a self-improving RLM agent (Prime Intellect)
signals.summary: Prime Intellect published Prime Agent, a self-improving reinforcement-learned agent. 253 pts on HN. Interesting research direction; not a build target for David.

signals.title: ProvenMetal (YC S26): circuit boards delivered in days instead of weeks
signals.summary: YC S26 Launch HN (234 pts): compresses PCB delivery from weeks to days. A read on where seed-stage hardware attention is going, not something in David's lane.

signals.title: Why Are Climate Investors So Disconnected Right Now?
signals.summary: Forbes piece (via GDELT) on a mood gap in climate-tech investing. The climate subwatch was otherwise quiet this week, mostly routine early-stage fund news. Logged for the climate-tech lens.

signals.title: Whodunnit AI: voice-driven murder mystery, interview AI suspects by voice
signals.summary: Show HN (125 pts): a consumer game where you interrogate AI suspects with your voice. Not David-fit, but a marker that real-time consumer voice UX is now good enough to carry a product. Logged as a voice-AI maturity data point.
